to.implementation_strategy: Build one demo slice using existing PF pipeline stages: feed a sample requirement through tech-spec generation, factory build, EAP, RDC, then the A3 packaging/signing path. Reuse /api/v1/backlog/groom/approve as the gate endpoint. Deliverables: scripted end-to-end demo artifact, automated check asserting the customer package contains zero raw .py, signed package checksum, and a gate rule that blocks normal feature work until the slice passes in CI.
conflict_findings: A7 is a gate over ALL feature work; running any parallel feature tasks concurrently risks rework if the slice exposes pipeline gaps.
Touches the same packaging pipeline as BI-PF-0398 - sequence strictly after it or coordinate.
duplication_findings: Packaging, signing, SBOM/LBOM and the NO-RAW-.py check are already specified in BI-PF-0398 (A3) - A7 must call that pipeline, not rebuild it.
Baseline 'one source for all editions / compiled-only shipping' policy from BI-PF-0387 must be reused as the rule the slice validates, not redefined.
Groom-approve endpoint already exists at /api/v1/backlog/groom/approve - reuse as the approval gate.
to.rationale: A7 is the integration proof and approval gate for Epic A. Reuse-first: every stage it exercises is already specified in sibling items (A3 packaging, 0387 baseline), so this item is orchestration, verification and a gate rule, not new pipeline code.
assumptions: A1/A2 slices and A3 packaging/signing exist or will exist before A7 is executed.
A representative requirement fixture exists to drive the demo slice.
CI can run the compiled package verification step.
'Customer package contains no raw .py' can be mechanically verified by scanning the package artifact.
risks: Gate blocks all downstream feature work - if the slice uncovers multi-week pipeline gaps, the entire roadmap stalls.
Demo slice may be tuned to pass while hiding real-world gaps (narrow happy path).
Signing keys and artifact storage may not be provisioned yet.
CI wiring for the end-to-end check may be missing.
missing_info: Which requirement/fixture to use as the vertical-slice demo.
Where signed demo packages are stored and retention policy.
Who signs off (single approver vs board) and what 'approval' formally unblocks.
Target environment for the EAP/RDC demo (air-gapped, cloud, local).
Exact timeout SLA for the end-to-end CI run.
